investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (used by Kata Containers peer-pods) had no remaining VM slots, and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 130–146 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service incident is present in the supplied packet.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled for 130–146 seconds with the scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector." The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (line 1905), which requires a kata peer-pod VM slot; because no slot was available and preemption found no victims, the pod never started, the agent was never created, and the expected evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) were never written, causing the contract validation to fail with all four fields missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the two nodes that carry that resource. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector for remote (kata peer-pod) workloads, and the 2 that do match have insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. As a result, every remote agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck in Unschedulable state and never reached a running phase, so the eval runner could not collect any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (used by Kata Containers peer-pods) had no remaining VM slots, and the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 130–146 seconds across all three sibling checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service incident is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence between 08:50 and 08:55 UTC on 2026-07-01 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node production cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the agent creation step, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were collected and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource exhausted or quota exceeded), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. This scheduling blockage prevented the eval runner from calling createAgent, so no runtime response was ever obtained and all required evidence fields remained empty. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
